Tight coupling occurs when a child object is created and accessed using a child-type reference.

blocks.text: Child c = new Child();

runs.text: Here, both the object type and the reference type are Child. The program directly depends on the specific child class.
2. What is loose coupling in Java?
coupling can be achieved by creating a child object and assigning its reference to a parent-type reference.

blocks.text: Parent ref = new Child();

runs.text: Here, the object is of type Child, but the reference is of type Parent. This allows the program to work with different child objects through the same parent-type reference.

Inheritance allows a child class to acquire accessible members from a parent class. It is implemented using the extends keyword.
The Child class inherits the accessible methods of Parent. It can use these methods without defining them again.

8. Why can a parent-type reference access inherited and overridden methods but not directly access specialized methods?

A parent-type reference can access the members declared in the parent class that are available through that reference. It can also invoke overridden instance methods, in which case Java executes the implementation belonging to the actual object.

However, a specialized method exists only in the child class and is not declared in the parent class. Therefore, the compiler does not allow the specialized method to be called directly through a parent-type reference.

Yes. Upcasting can be performed directly in one statement.

18. What happens when an object reference is passed to a method?
When an object reference is passed to a method, Java passes the value of that reference. The receiving parameter can then refer to the same object.
The parameter ref has the type Parent, but it refers to a Child object. Therefore, the overridden method in Child executes.
When a method accepts a parent-type parameter, it can work with multiple child objects without requiring a separate method for every child class.

22. What are the two types of polymorphism in Java?
Achieved through method overloading, where the compiler determines which overloaded method to call based on the method arguments.
Achieved through method overriding, where the implementation to execute is determined by the actual object's type at runtime.

23. What is compile-time polymorphism in Java?
Compile-time polymorphism occurs when the compiler determines which method implementation to call during compilation. Method overloading is a common example.
The compiler selects the appropriate overloaded method based on the number, types, and order of the supplied arguments.
24. What is method overloading in Java?
Method overloading means defining multiple methods with the same name in the same class but with different parameter lists.
The parameter lists can differ in:
The three methods share the name add, but their parameter lists differ. The compiler selects the appropriate method based on the arguments supplied.
Changing only the return type does not constitute method overloading.
25. What is the difference between method overloading and method overriding?
Method overloading defines multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists. Method overriding provides a new implementation of an inherited instance method in a child class.

rows: Usually occurs within the same class.

The method signature must match, with a compatible return type.
The compiler selects an overload based on the arguments.
The actual object's type determines the overridden implementation.
